title: Reliability Champion Handoff — 90-day Slate
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, actionable handoff playbook for Reliability Champions — engineers embedded within product teams who act as the primary SRE liaison for their service. The goal is to accelerate SLO adoption, reduce toil during launches, and create a repeatable 90-day ramp that surfaces operational risks early.

Audience:
- New Reliability Champions (first 90 days)
- Feature/product owners and tech leads
- Platform and SRE partners who will coach/run enablement

What this doc is (and is not):
- Is: a practical checklist + week-by-week tasks + communication templates + decision ledger for cross-team choices.
- Not: a formal governance contract (that lives in SLO registry/confluence). Use this as the tactical onboarding scaffold.

Success criteria (how we know champion onboarding worked):
- Champion completes the 90-day checklist and signs off with SRE coach.
- Service has an SLO with owner, monitoring, and an alert playbook (can be a simple 2-rule alert).
- One post-launch tabletop conducted with follow-ups tracked in Jira.
- Measured improvement in time-to-detect (TTD) for the service within 60 days.

High-level timeline (30/60/90 slices):
- Days 0–30 (Discover + Connect):
  - Meet SRE coach + product/tech lead.
  - Import service into SLO registry (if not present).
  - Baseline metrics: latency percentiles, error rate, traffic patterns, deployment cadence. Capture as a single snapshot doc.
  - Quick wins: add a dashboard with 4 tiles (p95 latency, error rate, TPS, recent deploys).
  - Deliverable: "Champion onboarding checklist v0" and shared channel created (#reliability-<service>).

- Days 31–60 (Instrument + Harden):
  - Define candidate SLO(s) with product input (consequences, user-visible impact).
  - Create alerting rules tied to the SLO (one-page runbook).
  - Run a dependency map session (identify upstream/downstream services and critical caches).
  - Performance experiment: run a 1-week load probe or replay if feasible.
  - Deliverable: SLO draft + alert playbook + dependency map artifact.

- Days 61–90 (Operate + Iterate):
  - Execute one tabletop incident scenario; capture root causes and runbook gaps.
  - Propose a small reliability experiment (e.g., add prefix caching for hot paths, enable KV cache fallback) and measure.
  - Finalize SLO and schedule quarterly review cadence.
  - Deliverable: 90-day signoff note and recommended next steps for long-term ownership.

Key stakeholders & roles:
- Champion (embedded engineer) — day-to-day owner for SLO ops and the runbook.
- Product/Tech Lead — defines acceptable user impact and approves SLO consequences.
- SRE Coach — provides templates, triage support, and final signoff.
- Observability/Platform — ensures dashboarding and alerting plumbing.
- Solutions Eng / Security if customer-facing with data/privacy implications.

Communication cadence (recommended):
- Weekly 30-minute sync (Champion + SRE coach) — progress, blockers, small decisions.
- Biweekly triage shadow (Champion watches SRE oncall for 1 shift).
- End-of-30/60/90 demo in the team’s weekly engineering meeting.

Templates (copy into the service folder):
- Slack starter: "Hey @here, creating #reliability-<service>. Champion: @<name>. Primary SRE coach: @<name>. This channel is for reliability notifications and small ops questions."
- SLO proposal template: one sentence objective, user impact examples, measurement window, target.
- Runbook stub: symptoms -> probable causes -> immediate mitigations -> postmortem tasks.

Sample SLOs (examples to copy/edit) — model-serving oriented but adaptable:
- Availability SLO (customer-facing inference endpoint): "99.9% successful responses (HTTP 200 with valid payload) over 30 days; measurement: synthetic + production success rate."
- Latency SLO: "P95 end-to-end request latency < 250ms over a rolling 14-day window for priority routes."
- Quality guardrail (optional): "Model response token-acceptance rate > 98% on validation prompts weekly."

Note: adapt windows/targets to user impact and contract (enterprise customers may require 99.95+).

Decision ledger (short-lived, lives in the service folder; use a single-line format):
- 2026-02-16 | Champion Maya | Chose P95 250ms for priority route | Rationale: product accepts slight tail latency in exchange for lower cost | Jira: SRE-4821
- 2026-02-28 | Product Lead Priya | Agreed to 99.9% availability | Rationale: enterprise pilot requires SLA-like promise | Jira: ENGOPS-127

Escalation matrix (quick-reference):
- Sev 1: page SRE-oncall -> champion -> tech lead -> exec oncall if customer-impacting >30m.
- Sev 2: Slack alert to #reliability-<service> with coach included.

Risk register (top 5):
- Missing dependency visibility (data plane calls to external partners) — mitigations: dependency map + shadowing.
- Alert fatigue — mitigations: start with minimal, measurable alerts and iterate.
- Incomplete instrumentation on private deployments — mitigations: run synthetic canary and network tests.
- Champion bandwidth — mitigations: timeboxed tasks + SRE pairing.
- Rollout regressions due to quantization changes — mitigations: staging perf tests + auto-fallback to higher-precision model variant.

Metrics dashboard (minimum tiles):
1) Request rate (TPS) with rolling 5m/1h windows
2) Error rate (5xx, model failure) with annotation for deploys
3) Latency histogram plus P50/P95/P99 markers
4) Recent deploys and commit id (link to CI/CD)

Playbook snippets (copy-and-paste friendly):
- On alert: 1) Acknowledge in alerting tool -> 2) Post initial assessment in channel (one-line: impact + hypothesis) -> 3) Execute immediate mitigation from runbook -> 4) Escalate if not resolved in 15m.

Operational experiments (first 90 days suggested):
- Prefix caching toggle test (measure token-level cost vs latency); run in canary for 48–72h.
- Batching policy test: increase batch size for non-interactive routes and observe latency tail.

Tabletop scenario (30–60m):
- Scenario: sudden model shard OOM due to high prompt size -> impact: 30% of requests fail with 503 -> actions: rollback quantized variant, route critical traffic to fallback region, scale pool by +1.
- Postgame: add a runbook step and define a preflight check for quantization changes.

Open questions / TODOs (actionable laundry list):
- [ ] Decide final SLO window for heavy tails (14d vs 30d) (owner: Product Lead Priya) — Jira ENGOPS-127
- [ ] Add synthetic canary for private deployments (owner: Platform Observability)
- [ ] Confirm oncall shadow schedule (owner: SRE Coach Liam)
- [ ] Create a one-click dashboard template in Grafana (owner: Observability team)

Appendix: quick links and references
- SLO registry canonical guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO-Registry
- Incident tabletop template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Tabletop-Template
- Oncall rota and SLAs: SRE-4821

Notes to self / draft signals:
- Keep the onboarding light and measurable; we want champions to ship a visible deliverable by day 30.
- Avoid starting with too many alerts — better to have one meaningful signal than ten noisy ones.
- Emphasize cross-team demos: show the dashboard to product early to align impact language.

Contact for questions: Maya Park (owner), SRE Coach Liam O'Connor.

Last edited: 2026-03-02 — internal draft for review by SRE coaches and platform observability.
